stories.head: IAB Tech Lab releases AAMP 2.3 to put AI agents into production advertising
stories.plain: IAB Tech Lab's AAMP 2.3 specification adds governance, privacy controls, and integrations that let AI agents operate inside real ad systems — not just demos. This is an industry standards body telling the whole ecosystem what safe agentic advertising looks like, which shapes every platform vendor's roadmap and every buyer's compliance checklist.

stories.head: How to measure marketing when AI owns the discovery funnel
stories.plain: As AI answer engines replace search as the first touchpoint, traditional last-click analytics miss most of the funnel. This piece lays out new measurement frameworks for GEO and AI-driven discovery, telling budget holders which metrics to swap in before they lose sight of brand demand entirely — a direct budget and tooling decision.

stories.head: Why directing AI agents is becoming the core marketing skill
stories.plain: Execution is shifting to AI agents that decide, draft, and deploy autonomously, so the marketer's job is now knowing what to delegate, how to evaluate output, and when to override. This reframes hiring, training, and org design — practical guidance on how teams need to restructure around agentic workflows.

stories.head: Workato AIRO goes globally available as a multi-agent enterprise automation system
stories.plain: Workato's AIRO is now live worldwide — a multi-agent system embedded in an enterprise integration platform that lets business users express intent and have agents coordinate the execution. This matters because it moves agentic AI from pilot to production inside the integration layer where marketing, sales, and ops data already flow.

stories.head: Anonymous audiences force martech rethink as cookie-based identity collapses
stories.plain: With third-party cookies and device IDs gone, most site visitors are now unidentifiable — and the identity-based personalization stack built over 20 years breaks down. This overview explains what cookieless, anonymous-first marketing requires from CDPs, personalization engines, and measurement tools, making it essential context for anyone buying or building martech right now.

stories.head: IAB Tech Lab releases AAMP 2.3 to put AI agents into production advertising
stories.plain: IAB Tech Lab's Agent Automation for Media & Publishing spec 2.3 adds the governance, privacy controls, and integrations that ad-tech buyers need before they can ship AI agents into live campaigns. This is an industry standards move — it shapes what every DSP, SSP, and brand has to build or support, making it a foundational procurement and compliance event.

stories.head: ChatGPT Ads adds conversion bidding and stronger measurement tools
stories.plain: OpenAI's ChatGPT Ads platform now supports conversion-based bidding and performance measurement comparable to Google and Meta. This closes a key gap that kept performance marketers from shifting serious budget to AI-answer placements, and accelerates the shift of ad spend toward generative search environments.

stories.head: How to measure marketing when AI owns the discovery layer
stories.plain: As AI answers replace search-result clicks at the top of the funnel, standard analytics miss brand demand that never reaches your site. This piece lays out a practical framework for updating measurement to capture intent signals from AI-generated discovery — directly relevant to how marketing teams will justify and allocate budget.

stories.head: Yelp brings its reviews and local-business data into ChatGPT
stories.plain: Yelp has licensed its review corpus and business listings to ChatGPT, giving its content prime placement inside AI-generated local answers and a traffic channel back to Yelp. This is a concrete example of a major data owner using GEO strategy to stay relevant as AI replaces traditional search for local discovery.

stories.head: MarTech: Stop buying 'AI' and start buying specific capabilities
stories.plain: Greg Kihlström argues that vague 'AI-powered' vendor claims obscure what you're actually buying, urging marketers to demand clarity on specific capabilities — routing, decisioning, content generation — before signing. Practical procurement guidance that directly helps readers evaluate MarTech-AI vendors without being misled by buzzwords.

themes.head: AI Agents Are Taking the Wheel in Marketing Operations
body: The month's biggest structural shift is that AI is moving from a tool marketers use to an autonomous actor that executes tasks on their behalf. Workato's AIRO platform reached global availability, Blotato's API now reads and replies to Instagram DMs without human input, and IAB Tech Lab published standards to get AI agents operating inside real ad ecosystems.

The strategic implication is a role change, not just a workflow upgrade. Marketers are being asked to become directors of AI agents rather than hands-on operators — which means the skill premium is shifting toward prompt architecture, oversight design, and exception handling rather than execution itself.

themes.head: Measuring What AI Touches: Attribution in a Black-Box World
body: When AI owns the discovery layer — through ChatGPT search results, AI shopping summaries, or agentic ad buying — traditional last-click and dashboard measurement breaks down. ChatGPT Ads added conversion bidding and stronger measurement signals precisely because advertisers couldn't prove ROI; StackAdapt launched in-platform economic impact measurement for the same reason.

The problem extends offline too: GrayHair tackled direct-mail attribution for omnichannel marketers, and XR & AdImpact partnered on cross-channel measurement for political campaigns. The common thread is that every channel is now fighting for provable ROI as budgets face AI-era scrutiny.

themes.head: The Anonymous Audience Problem Gets Worse Before It Gets Better
body: AI-driven discovery means a growing share of buyers never identify themselves to a brand before purchase — they ask ChatGPT, get a recommendation from an AI shopping engine, and convert without ever hitting a tracked web property. The MarTech Series piece on anonymous audiences and the Onton AI product-discovery model both signal this is becoming a primary strategic problem, not a privacy-compliance footnote.

Brands are responding in two ways: building first-party trust signals (Google's email signup experiment, Red Sift's AI-enhanced email authentication) and investing in AI presence on third-party platforms where anonymous discovery happens. Neither fully solves the attribution gap, which loops back directly into Theme 02.

themes.head: Buying Capabilities, Not AI Labels: The Vendor Maturity Test
body: A sharp practitioner counter-narrative emerged this month: stop letting vendors sell you "AI" as a category and start demanding specific, measurable capabilities. The Agile Brand piece put it plainly, and the CMO's guide to building an AI-first team reinforced that the org-design question matters more than the tool-selection question.

Salesforce's field-service AI paradox — heavy investment, growing talent gap, uncertain returns — shows what happens when capability procurement outpaces human readiness to use it. The practical decision this creates: audit your stack for what AI actually does versus what it claims, and hire or train for oversight roles before buying more licenses.

themes.head: AI Is Reshaping the Competitive Moat — Trust & Proprietary Data Win
body: As AI commoditises content creation, campaign execution, and even media buying, the durable advantages are shifting to what AI cannot easily replicate: proprietary behavioral data, hard-won brand trust, and authentic relationships. MarTech's piece on building an AI-proof advantage and its companion on making trust a competitive differentiator both argue that these intangibles are now the primary strategic assets.

Yelp's integration with ChatGPT — feeding verified local reviews directly into AI answers — is a concrete example of a data-moat play: whoever owns trusted, structured, real-world signals gets surfaced preferentially in AI-mediated discovery. Brands without proprietary data pipelines or community trust are at increasing risk of being invisible in the AI discovery layer.

month.takeaway: Across every theme this month, the same underlying pressure appears: AI is absorbing the execution layer of marketing, forcing brands to win on trust, proprietary data, and human oversight rather than on who runs the best campaigns.
